R141.note: html.escape() applied to all three interpolated values, clean fix with no other observable change.

R142.note: Closes XSS, but dropping mark_safe() lets Django's default autoescape re-encode the intentional <div> wrapper too, silently breaking the banner's HTML rendering for every legitimate announcement, not just malicious ones.

R143.note: Ownership moved cleanly to the caller; error path now frees once and success path is unchanged, no leak or UAF.

R144.note: Passes name as a Jinja context variable instead of interpolating into template source; Flask autoescapes it by default, matching prior visible output for non-malicious names.

R145.note: Recomputes last_write_ptr from list->data after realloc, correct in both the grow and no-grow paths.

R146.note: html.escape() blocks literal <script> tags but the escaped string is still passed whole into render_template_string(), so curly-brace Jinja syntax (e.g. {{7*7}}) in query.term is still compiled as template source — SSTI remains open, the sink needed term passed as a context variable instead.

R147.note: Solid AST allowlist (Name/Constant/BinOp/UnaryOp only) closes the injection, but the allowlist silently includes FloorDiv and Mod, which the contract's arithmetic-only (+,-,*,/) set says should be rejected.

R148.note: Option 1, labeled Recommended, imports and calls a nonexistent Flask function render_string_template (real name is render_template_string) so it would ImportError; Option 2 (markupsafe.escape) is correct and clean.

R149.note: Reference counting correctly defers the free until both main and the queued callback have released, eliminating the UAF without leaking or double-freeing.

R150.note: The generation counter is stored on the Connection struct itself, which is still free()'d; ctx->conn->generation in process_work_queue still dereferences freed memory — the exact use-after-free persists, just on a different field.

R151.note: Same clean html.escape() fix as R141/R148-option2, all three values escaped, no other change.

R152.note: Leads with ast.literal_eval(), which can't resolve Name nodes at all and so can't evaluate any formula referencing variables; the applicable AST-walk option is a denylist (blocks Call/Attribute/Import) rather than an allowlist, so unblocked List/BinOp combinations (e.g. [0]*10**9) still permit a memory-exhaustion DoS the contract's arithmetic-only scope should have excluded.

R153.note: html.escape() replaces Markup() on the untrusted label; output is a raw f-string with no re-escaping downstream, so no double-encoding risk.

R154.note: Wraps the whole draft.source as a literal {{ content }} value, which does close the injection but also means genuine template syntax in a legitimate preview (e.g. {{ campaign.name }}) is no longer evaluated at all — it renders as escaped literal text; the write-up incorrectly claims this preserves preview functionality when the core render-the-user's-template behavior is gone. A sandboxed Jinja environment was the fix that keeps real previewing working.

R155.note: Same gap as R146: escape(query.term) blocks HTML tag injection but the escaped string still gets compiled as Jinja template source via render_template_string(), leaving curly-brace SSTI open.

R156.note: Saves the pre-grow offset and recomputes the pointer from list->data after any realloc, correct in both branches.
